artists.biography: Brad formed officially in 1992, although the band members had been playing together for a long time before that. The band's line-up was composed of vocalist Shawn Smith, guitarist Stone Gossard, bassist Jeremy Toback, and drummer Regan Hagar. The band originally wanted to go by the name Shame, however the band found that the name was already taken by a band featuring musician Brad Wilson. Instead, the band took the name Brad and decided to name its debut album Shame. Shame, released on April 27, 1993 through Epic Records, was recorded in roughly 20 days, with many tracks taken from in-studio jam sessions. Shame, featuring a raw sound and an eclectic mix of styles, was released to mixed reviews and moderate sales. The track "20th Century" was a minor hit in the UK.

perplexity.description:
Released on April 27, 1993, Shame is the debut album by Brad, a Seattle-based rock band featuring Shawn Smith and Stone Gossard. The album stands out for its soulful, introspective blend of rock, funk, and singer-songwriter influences, diverging from the grunge-dominated sound of the era. Recorded in just twenty days at Avast Recording Co. in Seattle, Shame was produced by the band and mixed by Brendan O’Brien, resulting in a relaxed, emotive sound shaped by in-studio jam sessions. Its musical style draws from a deep well of soul, funk, and avant-garde elements, creating a cathartic and heartfelt listening experience.

Shame occupies a unique place in Brad’s discography as their foundational release, establishing their identity apart from the members’ other projects. While it arrived in the shadow of Pearl Jam’s commercial breakthrough, the album carved its own niche with its melodic depth and emotional honesty. Despite modest sales upon release and limited mainstream attention, Shame has since been recognized as an overlooked classic, praised for its sincerity and musical craftsmanship. Critics have noted its significance within the broader Seattle music scene, often comparing it favorably to other collaborative works like Temple of the Dog and Mad Season.
